recommendedTextbook.title: Modern Biology for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: S.T. Ramalingam
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education & NERDC

topics.topic: Biology and Living Organisms: Branches and Relevance
subtopics: Meaning of Biology and major branches (Zoology, Botany, Microbiology, Ecology, Genetics)
Scientific inquiry and biological drawing conventions (no shading, single sharp lines)
Relevance of biology to agriculture, medicine, pharmacy, and environmental conservation in Nigeria
objectives: Define biology and state five statutory rules of biological drawings for WAEC/NECO
Explain direct contributions of biological research to disease eradication and food security

topics.topic: Classification of Living Things: Kingdoms of Life
subtopics: Binomial nomenclature system (Linnaean hierarchy: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species)
The Five Kingdom Classification: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia
Diagnostic characteristics of Monera and Protista (Amoeba, Euglena, Paramecium)
objectives: State rules of writing scientific binomial names with correct capitalization and underlining
Compare diagnostic traits of the five biological kingdoms

topics.topic: Cell Structure, Organization of Life and Microscopy
subtopics: Plant and animal cell organelles and comparative ultrastructure
Levels of biological organization: Cells, tissues, organs, systems, and organisms
Compound optical microscope handling, magnification calculation, and slide preparation
objectives: Identify and diagram cell organelles with their physiological functions.
Differentiate plant and animal cells under high-power optical magnification.
Calculate linear magnification from biological microphotographs.

topics.topic: The Cell as a Living Entity: Levels of Biological Organization
subtopics: Levels of organization: cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system -> organism
Unicellular organisms functioning as independent living entities (Amoeba, Chlamydomonas)
Specialized tissues in plants (xylem, phloem, epidermal) and animals (epithelial, muscular, nervous, connective)
objectives: Identify levels of organization from organelle to multicellular organism
Explain physiological advantages of cell specialization in higher organisms

topics.topic: Cellular Physiology: Diffusion and Osmosis in Living Systems
subtopics: Mechanisms of diffusion and concentration gradients
Osmosis as a special case of diffusion across semi-permeable membranes
Plasmolysis, turgidity, flaccidity, hemolyis, and crenation
objectives: Demonstrate diffusion using potassium permanganate crystals in a beaker
Set up an osmometer using peeled Irish potato and sucrose solution
Explain biological significance of turgidity in herbaceous plant support

topics.topic: Nutrition in Plants: Photosynthesis and Mineral Nutrition
subtopics: Autotrophic nutrition: light and dark reactions of photosynthesis
Internal structure of a dicotyledonous leaf and adaptation for photosynthesis
Macro-nutrients and micro-nutrients required by plants and deficiency symptoms
objectives: Write chemical and word equations for photosynthesis
Perform laboratory starch test on a variegated leaf showing need for light and chlorophyll
Identify nitrogen and phosphorus deficiency symptoms in local maize crops

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Practical Laboratory Test
subtopics: Assessment on microscope usage, cell theory, osmosis, and photosynthesis
Hands-on WAEC alternative-to-practical test
objectives: Demonstrate practical proficiency in specimen drawing, staining, and biochemical testing

topics.topic: Nutrition in Animals: Holozoic Nutrition and Food Tests
subtopics: Heterotrophic nutrition modes (holozoic, parasitic, saprophytic, symbiotic)
Biochemical tests for carbohydrates (Benedict test, iodine test), proteins (Biuret, Millon), and fats (Sudan III, emulsion)
Balanced diet and caloric requirements for different occupations
objectives: Perform statutory WAEC biochemical food tests on unknown solutions with clear observation/inference tables
Distinguish reducing from non-reducing sugars

topics.topic: Digestive System and Enzymes: Mechanisms in Humans and Herbivores
subtopics: Structure of the human digestive tract and associated glands (liver, pancreas)
Enzymatic digestion of food along the alimentary canal
Ruminant digestive modifications (rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum in cattle)
objectives: Trace chemical digestion of starch, proteins, and lipids from mouth to ileum
State properties of biological enzymes (temperature, pH sensitivity, specificity)
Compare human monogastric digestion with polygastric digestion in Nigerian livestock

topics.topic: Transport System: Human Circulatory Anatomy & Heart Mechanics
subtopics: Need for transport systems in multicellular organisms
Internal anatomy of the mammalian heart (atria, ventricles, bicuspid/tricuspid valves, septum)
Double circulation (pulmonary and systemic loops) and blood pressure
objectives: Draw longitudinal section of mammalian heart with precise directional flow arrows
Differentiate arteries, veins, and capillaries structurally and functionally
Explain heart sounds (lub-dub) and cardiac cycle mechanics

topics.topic: Blood Physiology: Cells, Plasma and ABO Grouping
subtopics: Cellular components of mammalian blood (erythrocytes, leukocytes, thrombocytes)
Blood clotting cascade (thromboplastin, prothrombin, thrombin, fibrinogen, fibrin)
ABO and Rhesus blood grouping systems and transfusion safety
objectives: State functions of blood plasma and cellular elements in defense and transport
Outline biochemical steps in blood clot formation
Determine compatibility in blood transfusion donor-recipient matrices

topics.topic: Transport in Plants: Absorption and Translocation
subtopics: Absorption of water and mineral salts by root hairs (osmosis and active transport)
Upward movement of xylem sap (transpiration pull, root pressure, capillarity)
Translocation of manufactured food through phloem sieve tubes
objectives: Draw transverse section of dicot root and stem showing arrangement of vascular bundles
Explain cohesion-tension theory of transpiration pull
Demonstrate translocation using ringing experiments on tree trunks

topics.topic: Comprehensive Revision & Terminal WASSCE Mock Examination
subtopics: Syllabus revision of cells, physiological transport, and biochemical nutrition
Full examination administration, moderation, and feedback
objectives: Demonstrate complete mastery of SSS 1 Biology Term 1 curriculum
